analysis.one_liner: PFC is a Maharatna, government-owned NBFC that borrows in bulk and lends mainly to India's power sector - generation, transmission, distribution and increasingly renewable energy projects.
analysis.whats_happening: PFC reported Q2 FY27 (quarter to Sep 2026) results in early November: standalone net profit rose 11.8% YoY to about ₹4,987 crore, but the consolidated number (which folds in REC, a subsidiary) slipped roughly 2% to ₹7,681.51 crore as REC's performance dragged on the combined figure. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹4.10/share, with the ex-date set for 2026-11-17. Separately, and more consequentially, the merger of REC into PFC is moving forward: both exchanges and the RBI have issued no-objection certificates (RBI on 2026-10-15, NSE/BSE on 2026-10-19), the board-approved swap ratio is 88 PFC shares for every 100 REC shares, and completion is targeted for 2027-04-01.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of PFC as a government-backed bank that only lends to power projects - it borrows cheaply because the state stands behind it, and lends that money out at a spread. The tension right now is twofold: the stock looks statistically cheap (P/E near 4x, trading below book value) partly because PSU lenders always carry a valuation discount, but also because PFC is about to absorb its own peer, REC, in a near-11-lakh-crore-rupee merger whose final terms and timing are still not locked down. Standalone profit is growing nicely, but the number that includes REC actually fell last quarter - so the entity you'd be buying into is changing shape under your feet.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): standalone PAT ₹4,986.71 crore, up 11.8% YoY from ₹4,461.94 crore; consolidated PAT ₹7,681.51 crore, down about 2% YoY, with H1 FY27 consolidated profit at ₹16,679 crore. For context, FY26 standalone PAT was a record ₹20,051 crore (+16%) while consolidated FY26 PAT was ₹33,625 crore (+10%) - so the gap between standalone PFC and the REC-inclusive consolidated number is a recurring feature, not a one-off, and matters more now given the pending merger. Management has guided FY27 loan growth of roughly 10% and spreads of 2.40-2.50%, citing competitive lending conditions compressing margins slightly.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock has returned about 297% versus the Nifty's 38.5% - a large outperformance - but it is down 36.4% from its July 2024 peak of ₹517.26, and down nearly 21% in just the last 3 months, underperforming even its REC peer over that window. The two corporate actions on record (a 2016 2-for-1 split and a 2023 5-for-4 split) are ordinary splits, not demergers or spin-offs, so the price series is not understating returns here - the drawdown from peak is a genuine price decline, driven by sector de-rating and merger-related uncertainty, not a split artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: On screener-sourced numbers, PFC trades near P/E 4.1x and P/B 0.74x, with ROE around 20.7% and ROCE near 9.7% (other data providers show figures ranging P/E 3.2x-4.3x and P/B 0.7x-1.2x depending on the date and whether standalone or consolidated EPS is used - the cluster centers on roughly 4x earnings and below book value). Why it's cheap: PSU lenders to the power sector carry a structural valuation discount for perceived state-influenced lending decisions, plus near-term uncertainty from the REC merger. Whether it's actually cheap is less clear - a ~20% ROE and decade-low NPAs are the kind of numbers that would normally not trade this low, so part of the discount may be a genuine risk premium for leverage and merger execution risk rather than a market mispricing.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is volume-led: management guides to roughly 10% loan book growth in FY27, with spreads actually narrowing (guided 2.40-2.50%) due to competitive lending conditions - so margins are under mild pressure even as the book expands. The renewable energy loan portfolio (around ₹90,135-1,75,969 crore depending on standalone/group scope) has more than doubled in five years and is the fastest-growing, most diversifying part of the book, reducing reliance on legacy thermal and state-discom exposure.
analysis.health_read: As a lending institution, PFC's 'cash conversion' question is really an asset-quality and leverage question rather than a working-capital one. Asset quality has improved sharply - net NPA is reported near a 10-year low (figures from 0.13% to 0.37% depending on standalone vs consolidated scope), down from levels above 3% gross NPA a few years ago - so business risk from bad loans looks much reduced. The more structural concern is financial risk: PFC runs with debt/equity near 4.2x, which is normal for a wholesale lender of this kind but means earnings are sensitive to borrowing costs and any slip in asset quality gets amplified by leverage.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the President of India (Government of India), holding about 56% with zero pledging. Institutional ownership is substantial - FIIs around 17.8%, mutual funds around 9%, insurance around 6.2% - with retail holding roughly 10.5%. There is no marquee named private investor on the register to flag; this is a straightforward state-controlled, institutionally-held stock.
strengths: Standalone net profit grew 11.8% YoY to ₹4,987 crore in Q2 FY27, with FY26 standalone PAT at a record ₹20,051 crore (+16%)
Net NPA has fallen to a reported multi-year/decade low (0.13%-0.37% depending on scope), down from levels above 3% gross NPA a few years ago
ROE of roughly 20.7% and a dividend yield near 5.7%, among the higher-yielding large NBFCs
Renewable energy loan book has more than doubled over five years, diversifying away from legacy thermal and discom credit risk
watchpoints: Consolidated profit (which includes REC) fell ~2% YoY in Q2 FY27 even as standalone profit rose - a sign REC-side performance is weaker just as the two entities prepare to merge

The REC-into-PFC merger (88:100 share swap) still needs shareholder, creditor and possibly Ministry of Corporate Affairs approval, with completion targeted for 2027-04-01 - delay or changed terms is a live risk for current holders
Debt/equity near 4.2x is structural to the NBFC model but leaves earnings exposed to funding-cost swings and any reversal in asset quality

Stock is down 36.4% from its July 2024 peak and fell almost 21% in the last 3 months alone, underperforming its REC peer over that window - sentiment has been weak even as reported fundamentals improved
analysis.one_thing: Watch how the PFC-REC merger's final approvals and terms land, alongside whether consolidated (REC-inclusive) NPA and profit trends converge with PFC standalone's - that will determine the risk profile of the combined entity post-April 2027.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked profit figures, dividend, and merger timeline across multiple news sources (Business Upturn, HDFC Sky, Multibagg, TradingView/Quartr) and they agree on the core numbers. However, NPA percentages and P/E/P/B ratios vary meaningfully by source depending on whether standalone or consolidated (REC-inclusive) figures are used and the exact data date (P/E cited anywhere from 3.25x to 4.34x, P/B from 0.73x to 1.22x); this report uses the screener.in-sourced cluster (P/E ~4.1x, P/B ~0.74x) as the central estimate and flags the standalone-vs-consolidated NPA split explicitly rather than averaging it away. Exact current loan book composition and REC's standalone financials were not independently verified - check screener/company filings for REC-specific detail.
